column2: STYLE: text-mode ANSI art. Every pixel belongs to a character cell (draw your own tiny bitmap font, ~4x6 or 5x8 px cells, with CP437-style blocks, shades and box-drawing pieces), in the 16-colour EGA palette on black, no anti-aliasing. THEME: a NetHack-style dungeon. Each numeral is a dungeon room or corridor drawn in box-drawing walls, lit by torches, with the @ hero, letter monsters and items inside; on every beat the game takes one turn (everyone moves one cell, torches flicker). Minute turn: the hero takes the stairs and the new level is mapped in as the new digit. Hour: a dragon 'D' boss fight, the time still reading.

STYLE: risograph print. Three spot inks only (fluorescent pink, teal, yellow) overprinting where they cross to make the extra colours, coarse riso grain and halftone, each ink layer slightly misregistered and drifting a pixel or so, paper white showing through. THEME: carnivorous plants. Each numeral is a Venus flytrap or pitcher-plant vine grown into the digit's shape, traps snapping at flies on every beat, tendrils curling. Minute turn: the old plant wilts back and the new one sprouts and unfurls into the next digit. Hour: everything blooms at once, the time still reading.

STYLE: neon signage at night. Bent glass tubes of constant width with electrode ends and black-painted blockout where a tube crosses itself, a soft coloured glow round lit tubes on a dark brick wall, the hum and flicker of real neon, transformer cables. THEME: an old Hong Kong street sign. Each numeral is a neon tube with chase sequences running along it and its own sign animation on the beat (outlines stepping through a few positions like real animated neon). Minute turn: the tube sputters out section by section and the new digit buzzes on. Hour: the whole street of signs flashes its sequence, the time still reading.

STYLE: hand knitting. Every pixel is a knit stitch: a small V-shaped stitch texture on a grid of rows, Fair Isle colourwork in 3-5 yarn colours, slight unevenness of tension, a fuzzy halo of fibre. THEME: a winter jumper being knitted. Each numeral is a colourwork motif knitted into the fabric, the fabric breathing and stretching on the beat as the needles click, a ball of yarn rolling and feeding the work. Minute turn: the old digit is unpicked evenly (never top-down) and the needles knit the new one in. Hour: the whole jumper pattern changes, the time still reading.

STYLE: chalk on a green-black school blackboard. Dusty chalk strokes with broken grain, smudged eraser ghosts, a few coloured chalks, hand-drawn arrows. THEME: a coach's play diagram. Each numeral is a play drawn in X's and O's with route arrows, and the players run their routes along the digit's strokes on every beat (whistle, sprint, settle). Minute turn: the eraser wipes the old play and the coach chalks the new one, outline first. Hour: the big play, the whole team running, the time still reading.

STYLE: original Game Boy. Exactly four shades of DMG green, an 8x8 tile grid for the level, 8x16 sprites, hard pixels, no colour beyond the four. THEME: a side-scrolling platform game. Each numeral is level geometry built from bricks, pipes and question blocks, and a little hero runs and jumps across it, bumping a block on every beat (coins pop). Minute turn: the hero ground-pounds the old digit's blocks away and the new digit's blocks drop into place. Hour: a boss level, the time still reading. Scroll only the background, never the time.

STYLE: loose wet-on-wet watercolour. Transparent flat washes in pinks, coral and lagoon teal, soft blooms and hard dried edges where a wash pooled, white paper grain, a few dry-brush strokes. No 3D shading. THEME: a lagoon of flamingos. Each numeral is a flamingo (or two) whose neck, body and stilt legs bend into the digit's shape; on every beat they shift weight, dip their heads and flag their heads together like a real flamingo marching display. Minute turn: the old bird runs and lifts off, the new one glides in and settles into the next digit. Hour: the whole flock's marching display, the time still reading.

STYLE: manga page. Black ink, white paper, screentone dot fields, speed lines and focus lines, one spot colour (red) used sparingly, panel borders. THEME: the numerals ARE the giant hand-lettered sound effects of a fight scene: chunky, brushy SFX lettering that slams onto the page with impact lines on every beat, shaking and echoing. Minute turn: a punch shatters the old digit into ink shards and the new SFX slams in. Hour: a full-page splash panel, the time still reading.

STYLE: an antique engraved sea chart. Copperplate line engraving (hatching, stipple, rhumb lines from a compass rose, cartouches), hand-tinted with pale watercolour washes on aged paper. THEME: here be monsters. Each numeral is a sea serpent whose coils loop through the engraved waves in the digit's shape; the coils undulate on every beat, spouting, while a tiny galleon tacks between them. Minute turn: the old serpent dives and a new one surfaces as the next digit. Hour: the kraken rises, the time still reading.

STYLE: Chinese New Year woodblock print (nianhua). Bold black outlines, flat vermilion, gold, emerald and pink fills, auspicious cloud scrolls, woodblock grain. THEME: dragon and lion dance. Each numeral is a dragon's long body carried on poles by dancers whose legs show beneath it, rippling on every beat of the drum and cymbals as the head chases a pearl. Minute turn: the dragon writhes out of the old digit's shape and into the new one. Hour: firecrackers and a lion dance, the time still reading.

STYLE: cyanotype photogram. Prussian blue and white only with the tonal range of exposure (deep blue to pale), silhouettes of real objects laid on the paper, soft edges where they lifted, brush marks at the paper's edge. THEME: Anna Atkins' British Algae. Each numeral is a seaweed or fern frond laid in the digit's shape, swaying on every beat as if still in a tide pool, the light shifting across the print. Minute turn: the old specimen is lifted, the paper is washed and the new frond's print develops in. Hour: a full plate of specimens, the time still reading.

STYLE: Art Nouveau poster in the manner of Mucha. Whiplash curves, flat muted pastel and gold fills with fine dark outlines, a halo or mosaic disc, an ornamental frame, lilies. THEME: the numerals are the flowing hair of a muse: tresses sweep and curl into each digit's shape and ripple on every beat as in a breeze, lilies opening along them. Minute turn: the hair unfurls out of the old digit and sweeps into the new one. Hour: the whole poster blooms, the time still reading.

STYLE: American traditional tattoo flash. Heavy black outlines, flat red, green, yellow and skin tones, solid black shading blocks only (no gradients), banners and stars, a sheet of flash on yellowed paper. THEME: each numeral is a tattoo motif bent into the digit: a snake round a dagger, a swallow, an anchor rope, a rose stem; swallows flap and snakes flick tongues on the beat of the buzzing machine. Minute turn: the machine re-inks: the new digit's outline is lined in, then coloured. Hour: the whole sheet comes alive, the time still reading.

STYLE: 1966 San Francisco psychedelic concert poster. Hand lettering that swells and warps to fill its space, vibrating complementary colours (red on green, orange on blue) side by side at full saturation, flat fills, wavy outlines. THEME: the numerals are the poster's melting, flowing letters themselves, pulsing and rippling on every beat while the colours vibrate and swap. Minute turn: the old digit melts and flows into the new one. Hour: the whole poster's colours cycle, the time still reading. Legibility is the hard part: keep the digits readable.

STYLE: a child's crayon and felt-tip drawing on lined notebook paper, with line boil: every line is redrawn with a slight wobble about 12 times a second, like a hand-drawn animation, scribbled waxy fills that don't stay inside the lines. THEME: the numerals are doodle monsters the kid drew: googly eyes, teeth, little legs, each digit's shape is the monster's body; on every beat they stomp, roar and wiggle. Minute turn: the old monster gets scribbled out or runs off the page and the new one is drawn in. Hour: a monster party, the time still reading.

STYLE: 1930s Art Deco travel poster. Flat airbrushed colour bands in the sky, bold simplified shapes, limited palette, a strong sun or radiating rays, a little title lettering. THEME: an aerobatic display team: little planes trail coloured smoke and the smoke trails ARE the numerals; the planes keep looping round their digits, re-drawing them so the smoke billows fresh on every beat. Minute turn: the old smoke drifts and dissolves while the planes write the new digit. Hour: a full formation display, the time still reading.
